## Critique
- claim-1: Not established. Equation (3) is asserted rather than obtained from a displayed bordered matrix. Its factors have sizes \(b\) and \(j+a\), so an ordinary Laplace expansion would require a matrix of size \(j+a+b\), yet only the target \(j\times j\) Jacobi–Trudi matrix is displayed. No row sets, column sets, complementary minors, vanishing-minor argument, or reduction of the bordered determinant to the target determinant is supplied. Consequently the claimed “fixed border” sign \((-1)^{|\rho|}\) is unsupported; the full Laplace sign \((-1)^{\sum R+\sum C}\) was not computed. Moreover, the stated hypotheses allow \(b>i\), when \((i^j,\sigma)\) need not be a partition. For example, \(i=1,j=2,a=1,b=2,\rho=(2)\) produces \((1,1,2)\). Either \(b\le i\) must be assumed, as in the intended \(b=\min(i,j)\) setting, or generalized Jacobi–Trudi functions for integer sequences must be explicitly defined.
- claim-2: The observations for \(\rho=\varnothing\) and \(a=0\) are correct with the \(0\times0\) determinant convention, but they do not repair claim-1. For \(b=j\), the trailing block is indeed empty, but if ordinary Schur notation is intended one still needs \(j=b\le i\).
- claim-3: Not established as written because claim-1 remains unproved. In addition, \(J_v\to J_v/A_+J_v\) is not a quotient map defined on arbitrary elements of \(A\); one must first prove every displayed term lies in \(J_v\). The actual quotient consequence was omitted: for every proper \(\sigma\subsetneq\rho\), \(\omega(s_{\rho/\sigma})\) has positive degree, so its product lies in \(A_+J_v\), and the projected identity should reduce to
  \[
  [\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}]
  =(-1)^{|\rho|}
  [\bar s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})}].
  \]
  No assertion that \(\omega\) itself descends to \(A\) is justified unless the relevant rectangle is preserved.

## Repair certificates
- [proof-attempt] Supply one explicit bordered matrix with ordered rows and columns; prove its determinant reduces, with sign, to the target \(j\times j\) Jacobi–Trudi determinant; define both Laplace index sets \(R_\sigma,C_\sigma\) and their complements for every \(\sigma\subseteq\rho\); identify the two complementary minors with \(s_{\rho'/\sigma'}\) and \(s_{(i^j,\sigma)}\); prove all other minors vanish; and compute \((-1)^{\sum R_\sigma+\sum C_\sigma}\), including every row/column permutation and the fixed-border sign.

## Required revisions
- Add \(b\le i\), or explicitly define and justify generalized Schur functions for nonpartition sequences.
- Replace the unsupported equation (3) with the complete bordered-matrix Laplace calculation.
- Record the \(0\times0\) conventions and treat \(\rho=\varnothing\), \(a=0\), and \(b=j\) within that calculation.
- Only after proving the identity in \(\Lambda\), prove membership in \(J_v\), project to \(A\), and derive the simplified relation in \(J_v/A_+J_v\).
- State explicitly that the requested target is currently **not established** by the specialist output.
